## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The sixteenth rule of the *Nissaggiya Pācittiya* section in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Vinaya Piṭaka is titled *Eḷakaloma* ("Carrying wool too far"). It stipulates that a Buddhist monk who carries sheep's wool on an excessively long journey must relinquish the wool and formally confess the transgression. A complete modern English translation of the rule and its exposition is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
